questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Transactions and ACID”?
options: The query returns Ada and 42 in two columns.
SQLite often runs inside the application; MySQL and PostgreSQL commonly run as separate server processes.
Both updates are committed together in the same transaction.
Start with a small, readable SELECT query; connect it to an application only after you understand its result.
questions.answer: Both updates are committed together in the same transaction.
questions.explanation:
Both updates are committed together in the same transaction.
Why: A transaction groups several changes into one logical unit. COMMIT confirms them; ROLLBACK undoes them. ACID means atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability. SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate point inside a transaction, and ROLLBACK TO can undo changes made after it. Isolation levels and locking determine how concurrent changes are handled, and behavior varies by DBMS. For example, debiting one account and crediting another must succeed together.
